items.title: Canonical usage truth, ownership, and provider evidence are explicitly separated
items.statement: The prologue establishes immutable canonical UsageRecord aggregation, shared runtime attribution, provider-specific evidence classes, source-qualified GUI labels, canonical placement, durable pressure/switch history, and rollup-backed retention behavior while keeping provider/runtime facts outside Usage ownership.

evidence.exact_quote: - Usage events are emitted by tool invocation and aggregated into usage records.
- Usage records are immutable once committed; corrections require a new record with explicit versioning.

- Usage owns canonical UsageRecord aggregation and display semantics; History, Ledger, Orchestrator, and runtime-artifact consumers consume the same durable event family instead of defining parallel usage schemas.

- Rollup freshness: 5h/7d windows are served from redb rollups, not from raw event scans. Background analytics jobs refresh rollups incrementally; UI shows the last committed rollup plus an explicit freshness cue when a refresh is in progress.

items.impact: This is a strong ownership and truth-source baseline for downstream builders.
items.builder_discretion: none on canonical source precedence, provider/source labeling, and ownership boundaries

items.title: Usage envelope, rollup source, and routing identity are addressable
items.statement: UF-002 through UF-004 make Usage a first-class implementation-agnostic GUI feature, bind its values to seglog-derived redb rollups rather than usage.jsonl, and require object-first project/run/package/lane and usage_event_ref routing instead of timestamp, tier, or thread shortcuts.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The Usage feature is a first-class app/GUI area that remains a plan-only, implementation-agnostic specification for quota visibility, plan type, ledger inspection, analytics, and alerts, including 5h/7d usage and plan type where available.

canonical_text: Usage reads 5h/7d, dashboard, and analytics values from redb rollups produced by analytics scan jobs over the canonical seglog pipeline, with Tantivy search/projector support where applicable; usage.jsonl remains a human-readable mirror or compatibility input, not the canonical rollup source.

canonical_text: Usage storage and routing are scoped by canonical project, run, package, lane, UsageRecord, runtime object identity, usage_event_ref, and Ledger/Usage route targets rather than legacy timestamp/thread/tier shortcuts.

items.impact: The feature envelope and canonical data/routing boundaries are explicit.
items.builder_discretion: bounded to implementation mechanics that preserve the named sources and identities

items.title: Export, trust, account, widget, quota, ledger, and chat contracts are preserved
items.statement: UF-005 through UF-011 distinguish export classes, preserve projection-trust and blocked ownership, retain switch/pressure lineage, constrain widget consumers, expose source-qualified quota and ledger analytics, and route thread detail through an explicit context-circle interaction rather than a second Usage surface.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Usage export semantics stay distinct: record export returns exact record envelopes with stable ids, canonical ids, refs, metadata, and schema-aware payloads; bundle export packages records, Evidence, blobs/files, selected-object bundles, manifests, and run-history artifacts; view export produces filtered tables, charts, CSV/JSON summaries, search results, analytics views, and graph renders without becoming canonical record truth.'

canonical_text: Usage must preserve projection trust, action gating, blocked/runtime recovery ownership, attention-center rows, freshness labeling, and advisory quiet-window behavior without hiding canonical blocked or approval-wait episodes.

canonical_text: Usage attribution preserves account switch and pressure history through actor-scoped snapshots, account_switch_event and account_pressure_episode records, and explicit bridge precedence where attempt_id is the local runtime anchor, provider_attempt_ref? is provider/runtime trace, usage_event_ref is the Usage bridge, and receipt refs are external side-effect lineage.

canonical_text: 'Usage consumes widget and shell presentation contracts without re-owning them: Widget_System broad pre-rewrite Orchestrator widget material is compatibility lineage, dashboard_layout migration reads yield to widget_layout:v1:dashboard, and project-card usage copy stays compact with one primary and one secondary line.'

canonical_text: Usage surfaces show quota and plan visibility with 5h and 7d windows, detected/configured plan type, always-visible limits, background refresh, live vs after-run source disclosure, approaching-limit warnings such as 80%, and rate-limit-hit actions to switch platform or pause.

canonical_text: Usage keeps event-level usage ledger inspection, filtering/export, optional analytics by time/platform/project/tier, cost tracking/attribution, retention/privacy controls, and drill-down without turning filtered exports into canonical history.

canonical_text: Thread-scoped Usage appears as the chat context circle with hover-revealed Usage, Tokens, Cost, and More Details actions plus explicit click-to-Compact Now behavior; More Details opens the editor-tab Context Detail Pane, Compact Now dispatches only after explicit choice and exposes failure/degraded feedback, and app-wide Usage remains a separate surface.

items.impact: The segment preserves a broad, coherent feature contract; adversarial omissions are recorded separately.
items.builder_discretion: none where exact export, identity, ownership, and surface-routing semantics are named

items.title: Inspector, projection health, schema aliases, cost, blocking, fallback, and refresh are addressable
items.statement: UF-033 through UF-039 define object-first inspector routing, projection-health and quiet-window rules, canonical alias normalization, cost precision boundaries, blocked escalation observability, missing-secret fallback labels, and rate-limited refresh behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Artifact drill-through and receipt lineage use attempt_id, provider_attempt_ref, usage_event_ref, receipt refs, and explicit inspector_target values for details/evidence/usage/lineage, avoiding timestamp heuristics, tier_id pivots, eager deref, and feature-local routing semantics.

canonical_text: Usage help, notification, quiet-window, projection-health, and sensitive-action behavior routes notifications by severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, and projection trust; quiet windows apply only to advisory warnings; degraded projections expose current/refreshing/stale/degraded/unavailable states and record-backed fallback.

canonical_text: UsageRecord schema expectations preserve unified schema alias lineage such as usage_id, usage_source_kind, provider_runtime_usage, provider_quota_api, provider_usage_api, provider_error_hint, project_rollup, local-estimated, API-key-derived, and OAuth-quota-derived source detail, but those aliases normalize into usage_record_id, source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, provider/usage/quota projections, and UF-085 fields before persistence, aggregation, GUI projection, or route/open drill-through.

canonical_text: Usage cost display uses clamp/derived-field precision rules derived from cost_microdollars or exact provider minor-unit receipts, including <$0.01 = 6dp, <$1 = 4dp, otherwise 2dp, while cost_usd is display/migration material and raw provider cost values remain provenance/debug evidence only.

canonical_text: Usage blocked-state observability preserves attention_required, blocked_notice, blocked_family, allowed_action_ids[] stale-token retirement, escalation_level, action_available ownership, an 8-kind blocked-owner taxonomy, and a 5-level escalation ladder across Orchestrator, Dashboard, thread badges, and notifications.

canonical_text: When platform APIs require secrets such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, Usage must label missing live data honestly and always show project-local canonical usage summaries from rollups/projections as fallback.

canonical_text: Usage refreshes provider API data at reasonable cached intervals, supports explicit Refresh, updates from run results when available, and avoids excessive polling that could hit rate limits or consume quota.

items.impact: The segment exposes the intended canonical behaviors; several adversarial edge contracts remain incomplete and are itemized below.

items.title: Cost-bearing destructive actions and bulk receipts have explicit reversibility disclosure
items.statement: The prologue explicitly requires pre-execution disclosure for non-reversible and non-undoable actions, records undo-window semantics, and preserves parent/child bulk results instead of flattening partial failures.

evidence.exact_quote: Reversibility and undo disclosure is part of user-facing `/accounting` for cost-bearing actions. Receipts and confirmations classify each action as immediately undoable, reversible with a compensating action, non-reversible but confirmable, or destructive and `non-undoable`; user copy may also show `non-reversible` when no practical reversal exists. If `/undo` exists, the UI records the undo-window duration, whether the undo is `local-only` or `remote-compensating`, what invalidates it, and whether a background refresh, `/poll`, or subsequent mutation closes the window. Non-reversible and non-undoable actions must disclose that before execution rather than only in `/history`.

Bulk-operation receipts preserve the parent/child shape for usage and history. A parent bulk receipt carries aggregate counts for `/failed/blocked/skipped` plus completed targets; child receipts carry `per-target` result, usage_event_ref, rollback or `/undo` expectation, and any blocked reason. Orchestrator and history must not flatten a bulk action into one ambiguous line item.

items.impact: Builders have concrete disclosure and partial-failure requirements for destructive or bulk cost-bearing actions.
items.builder_discretion: none on pre-execution disclosure and parent/child receipt preservation

items.title: Provider source confidence and unknown reset states cannot be fabricated
items.statement: UF-023 explicitly distinguishes authoritative native quota, authoritative session/tool stats, and inferred usage, and requires unknown reset/cooldown copy instead of fabricated countdowns.

- Known reset/cooldown times tick live; unknown values render `Unknown reset` or `Unknown cooldown end`, never a fabricated countdown.

items.impact: This directly prevents misleading precision in provider rows.
items.builder_discretion: none on confidence classes and unknown reset wording

- `window_label`
- `window_scope: provider | account | account+model | org | server_profile`
- `unknown` means the UI may show inferred/estimated usage only if it labels the evidence source and avoids pretending to know reset semantics.

items.statement: The plan correctly says a generic 5h/7d column is misleading, yet UF-009 canonically requires always-visible 5h and 7d windows without conditioning them on provider availability or mapping them through window_kind/window_label. A builder can satisfy UF-009 literally and violate the generic usage-window contract.

items.title: Optional alerts.jsonl would reintroduce a parallel usage-side state owner
items.statement: The enhancement permits a separate alerts file even though the canonical pipeline requires one UsageRecord write/read model and classifies usage.jsonl as a mirror. It does not say whether alert episodes are canonical events, projections, retention-coupled records, or compatibility-only data.

evidence.exact_quote: - Optional; store in a small log or append to a file under `.puppet-master/usage/` (e.g. `alerts.jsonl`). Display in Usage or Settings.

- Unify on one canonical write path and one `UsageRecord` schema. If `usage.jsonl` persists, it is a mirror / compatibility artifact rather than an independent canonical source.
  - Document the schema in STATE_FILES and in code; use the same types for write and read where possible.
  - Prefer one projector/reader path for local summaries so Ledger, rollups, and UI projections do not fork into separate attribution models.

items.impact: Alert history can drift from pressure episodes, retention, and Usage projections or leak beyond canonical deletion policy.
items.builder_discretion: none; alert history must be assigned to a canonical event family or explicitly retired as an implementation option

items.title: Retention and privacy controls lack deletion, archive, and recovery semantics
items.statement: The plan names a 90-day raw-event policy, compaction, optional export-first behavior, and retention/privacy controls, but it does not define who can change retention, whether archive is encrypted, whether deletion reaches projections/blobs/exports, how legal or audit holds behave, or how interrupted compaction rolls back.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Retention policy: keep raw seglog events for a configurable window (default 90 days); archive or compact older events with an optional export-first step.
  - Seglog compaction: periodic background job consolidates older fine-grained events into daily summary records, reducing scan time while preserving attribution fidelity.
  - Rollup freshness: 5h/7d windows are served from redb rollups, not from raw event scans. Background analytics jobs refresh rollups incrementally; UI shows the last committed rollup plus an explicit freshness cue when a refresh is in progress.
  - `usage.jsonl` is a human-readable mirror only and MUST NOT be used for aggregation, rollup computation, or 5h/7d window serving. If retained for debugging, it follows the same retention policy as seglog.

canonical_text: Usage keeps event-level usage ledger inspection, filtering/export, optional analytics by time/platform/project/tier, cost tracking/attribution, retention/privacy controls, and drill-down without turning filtered exports into canonical history.

items.impact: Sensitive usage and identity data can survive inconsistently across raw events, rollups, mirrors, blobs, archives, and exports.
items.builder_discretion: none for deletion propagation, compaction atomicity, archive protection, and retention authority

items.title: Users can remove every Usage widget despite an always-visible/default contract
items.statement: The widget addendum allows every widget to be removed and only guarantees a nonempty first load. It does not preserve a required quota/status widget, define an empty-state recovery action, or reconcile removal with the success criterion that 5h/7d is always visible.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Remove** widgets they don't want to see.
The Usage page ships with this default layout. No page starts empty. Users can customize after first load.
- Usage section aligns with ecosystem norms: **always-visible** 5h/7d (and plan where available), plus optional analytics/cost view (yume/openclaudecto-style).

items.impact: A valid customization path can produce a blank or noncompliant Usage page with no obvious way to recover essential status.
items.builder_discretion: none; canon must define minimum widgets or an accessible empty-state restore path

items.statement: The only responsive rule bottoms out at two columns below 1200px. No phone-width one-column breakpoint, minimum card width, overflow behavior, touch reordering, or reduced-density fallback is defined.

evidence.exact_quote: - Column count is responsive: 2 columns (<1200px), 3 columns (1200-1600px), 4 columns (>1600px) per Plans/FinalGUISpec.md section 12.3.

items.impact: Narrow windows, mobile/WASM surfaces, zoomed layouts, and long localized labels can overflow or become unusable.
items.builder_discretion: bounded only after a canonical one-column/min-width/overflow rule is added

items.title: usage_id normalization is source-dependent without a deterministic discriminator
items.statement: The prologue says usage_id resolves to usage_record_id or usage_event_ref according to the importing source, and UF-035 requires normalization before persistence and routing, but no source discriminator or rejection rule decides which target applies when both or neither are present.

evidence.exact_quote: - `usage_id` resolves to `usage_record_id` or `usage_event_ref` according to the importing source; UI routes prefer `usage_event_ref` normalized through `object_kind = usage_event` and `object_id`.

canonical_text: UsageRecord schema expectations preserve unified schema alias lineage such as usage_id, usage_source_kind, provider_runtime_usage, provider_quota_api, provider_usage_api, provider_error_hint, project_rollup, local-estimated, API-key-derived, and OAuth-quota-derived source detail, but those aliases normalize into usage_record_id, source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, provider/usage/quota projections, and UF-085 fields before persistence, aggregation, GUI projection, or route/open drill-through.

items.impact: Imports can attach usage to the wrong object or create nondeterministic deep links and duplicate records.
items.builder_discretion: none; source discriminator, both/neither handling, and deterministic precedence must be specified

items.title: Cost display precision omits rounding, sign, overflow, currency, and locale rules
items.statement: UF-036 defines decimal places at USD thresholds, but not rounding mode, negative credits/refunds, zero, very large values, integer overflow, non-USD minor units, decimal separators, currency placement, or accessible spoken labels.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Usage cost display uses clamp/derived-field precision rules derived from cost_microdollars or exact provider minor-unit receipts, including <$0.01 = 6dp, <$1 = 4dp, otherwise 2dp, while cost_usd is display/migration material and raw provider cost values remain provenance/debug evidence only.

items.impact: Ledger, export, and GUI can disagree by rounding or misrender credits, currencies, and localized values.
items.builder_discretion: none for rounding mode, exceptional values, currency normalization, and locale/accessibility formatting

items.title: allowed_action_ids[] is simultaneously current and retired
items.statement: The prologue says blocked/recovery flows use ordered allowed_action_ids[] and only allowed_actions[] is legacy, but UF-037 labels allowed_action_ids[] itself as a stale-token disposition. These statements cannot both guide a builder or validator.

evidence.exact_quote: Small-sweep owner precedence is explicit for these hidden cross-cutting contracts. `usage-feature.md` owns cost_usage routing and cost attribution; `newtools.md` owns Docker/Actions readiness and deprecated-alias doctor IDs; Crosswalk owns `/precedence` between feature-owner docs; Docker, GitHub Actions, and Orchestrator owners keep their operational IDs rather than duplicating cost rules here. References hidden in `Crosswalk.md`, `newtools.md`, or `usage-feature.md` are still canonical when they are the named owner, including `/Docker/Orchestrator` readiness/cost links and `deprecated-alias` handling. Legacy `allowed_actions[]` remains compatibility-only; blocked/recovery flows use ordered `allowed_action_ids[]` without accidental global find/replace.
- allowed_action_ids[] is preserved as a stale-token disposition in this usage-side carry-through span.

items.impact: Implementations may delete the live blocked-action field or preserve a field validators expect retired, breaking recovery actions across surfaces.
items.builder_discretion: none; canon must explicitly retire allowed_actions[] while retaining or replacing allowed_action_ids[] consistently

items.title: Secret-dependent provider data has labels but no secure secret lifecycle
items.statement: UF-038 tells the UI to mention ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN and provide fallback data, but does not define secure acquisition, storage source, scope, permission checks, redaction in raw payloads/logs/exports, rotation, revocation, or distinction between missing and invalid credentials.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When platform APIs require secrets such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, Usage must label missing live data honestly and always show project-local canonical usage summaries from rollups/projections as fallback.

items.impact: Secrets can leak through usage diagnostics or be applied at the wrong project/account scope, while invalid credentials can be mislabeled as merely absent.
items.builder_discretion: none for secret source, scope, redaction, rotation/revocation, and credential-state taxonomy

items.title: Refresh lacks coalescing, backoff, offline, cache-scope, and stale-response rules
items.statement: UF-039 requires reasonable cached intervals and explicit Refresh, but does not define one in-flight request per provider/account, rate-limit backoff and jitter, cancellation, offline versus missing-secret versus provider-error states, cache partitioning, response ordering, or whether an older response may overwrite a newer run-derived update.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Usage refreshes provider API data at reasonable cached intervals, supports explicit Refresh, updates from run results when available, and avoids excessive polling that could hit rate limits or consume quota.

- 5-15 min
- cache last result
- Refresh
- After each run
- rate limits
- API errors
negative_constraints:
- Polling usage endpoints too frequently must not consume user quota or cause blocked requests.

items.impact: Refresh storms can consume quota, cross-account cache leakage can expose data, and late responses can regress visible usage or eligibility.
items.builder_discretion: none for request coalescing, ordering, backoff, cache partitioning, offline taxonomy, and stale-response rejection

items.title: On-demand inspector dereference has no unavailable, unauthorized, or hostile-blob behavior
items.statement: UF-033 correctly forbids eager dereference, but does not define the UI and audit result when a ref is deleted, corrupt, too large, unauthorized, from an untrusted provider, or changes between row render and click.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Artifact drill-through and receipt lineage use attempt_id, provider_attempt_ref, usage_event_ref, receipt refs, and explicit inspector_target values for details/evidence/usage/lineage, avoiding timestamp heuristics, tier_id pivots, eager deref, and feature-local routing semantics.
- History inspector deref policy is on-demand only, never eager.

items.impact: Click-to-expand can disclose unauthorized content, hang on huge blobs, or silently show stale/corrupt evidence.
items.builder_discretion: none for authorization, integrity checks, size limits, stale-ref handling, and user-visible failure states

items.title: Projection-health labels lack transition and recovery oracles
items.statement: UF-034 lists current, refreshing, stale, degraded, and unavailable and requires record-backed fallback, but does not define entry/exit conditions, freshness thresholds, concurrent refresh precedence, whether stale can still authorize sensitive actions, or which evidence proves recovery.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Usage help, notification, quiet-window, projection-health, and sensitive-action behavior routes notifications by severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, and projection trust; quiet windows apply only to advisory warnings; degraded projections expose current/refreshing/stale/degraded/unavailable states and record-backed fallback.

items.impact: Different consumers can disagree on health, sensitive actions may execute from stale projections, and the UI can claim recovery without current evidence.
items.builder_discretion: none for transition predicates, sensitive-action gating, freshness thresholds, and recovery evidence

highest_risk_gaps: Raw payload inspection lacks redaction and trust/access boundaries
Immutable correction records lack supersession and idempotency semantics
allowed_action_ids[] is simultaneously current and retired
Secret-dependent provider data has no secure secret lifecycle
Refresh lacks coalescing, cache partitioning, backoff, and stale-response rejection
synthesis.cross_cutting_conclusion: The assigned Usage plan has unusually strong source, owner, provider, and GUI-placement separation, but it is not yet implementation-deterministic at several stateful and security-sensitive seams. The critical blockers are not missing feature breadth; they are contradictory blocked-action vocabulary and absent executable contracts for sensitive payloads, corrections, secrets, and concurrent refresh. Accessibility, data lifecycle, export security, migration, pricing, and projection-state oracles also require canonical decisions rather than builder inference.
